# Plan Your Next Holiday: Create a Custom Travel Itinerary with Meta AI

**Hook:** By the end of this guide you'll have a draft day-by-day holiday plan built around your dates, budget and the kinds of places you actually enjoy — no travel agent needed. This is for anyone with a trip in mind who dreads the blank-page problem of "where do I even start?". One honest note up front: Meta AI can brainstorm the plan and suggest places, but it can't book flights, hotels or restaurants for you, and details like opening hours or ticket prices may drift out of date — always double-check before you go.

## Before you start

- **A free Meta account** — the same one you use for Facebook, Instagram or WhatsApp. If you don't have one, you can sign up at meta.ai with just an email. Meta AI itself is free on the standard plan.
- **A phone or a computer** with internet access. Meta AI works in any modern browser at meta.ai, and inside the Meta apps on both iPhone and Android.
- **Roughly 10–15 minutes** of uninterrupted time, plus a few quick notes on your own preferences — when you're going, who you're travelling with, what you enjoy. A notes app nearby helps.

## Step 1 — Open Meta AI and start a new chat

Pick the route that matches where you are right now. The simplest is on a computer: open any modern browser and go to **meta.ai** — that's the official Meta AI website. After you sign in with your Meta account (Facebook, Instagram or WhatsApp all work), a clean chat window opens with a text box at the bottom that says something like "Ask Meta AI…" — that's where the planning starts. On a phone, you have three clear options. **In WhatsApp**, open the app and look at the very top of the Chats tab for a circular blue icon (a chat bubble with a sparkle) labelled "Meta AI" — tap it once. **In Facebook**, tap the magnifying glass search icon at the top of the app, type "Meta AI" into the search bar, then tap the official Meta AI result from the list. **In Instagram**, tap the messenger icon (the paper-airplane shape) at the top right of the home screen, then look along the top of your message list for a "Meta AI" banner. Each route lands you on the same chat screen once you're signed in. If the icon isn't where described, the easiest fallback is the website: meta.ai works on every device, every account, and never needs an app update. If the website won't load, try a different browser, or check that you're signed into your Meta account. **You'll know it worked when** you see an empty chat with the text "Ask Meta AI" or a similar prompt at the bottom, and your profile picture at the top.

## Step 2 — Send your first travel prompt

Tap inside the text box at the bottom of the chat and write one clear first message covering the basics: where you want to go, when, how long, and who's coming. The more useful detail you give upfront, the more tailored the draft — think of it like briefing a friend who's planning alongside you. After you tap the paper-plane send icon (or press Enter on a computer), Meta AI usually replies within seconds with a written day-by-day outline. If a small spinner shows instead, wait — longer answers can take 10–20 seconds. The free plan lets you send many messages a day; if you ever see a "too many messages" notice, wait an hour or switch to a different Meta app and continue. **You'll know it worked when** a chunk of text appears below your question with headings like "Day 1", "Day 2" and so on.

💬 Example: *"Plan a 5-day trip to Kyoto for two adults in early November. We like quiet temples, walking and local food. Mid-range budget, flying in and out of Osaka."*

## Step 3 — Refine the plan with a follow-up question

Treat the first reply as a starting draft, not the final answer. Read it, then ask one specific follow-up that pushes the plan closer to what you actually want — swap a busy day for a slower one, add a rest afternoon, or shift the budget. Type the question into the same text box and send; Meta AI keeps the whole conversation in mind, so each new answer builds on the last rather than starting over. If the reply misses the mark, rephrase with more detail — instead of "make it cheaper", try "cut Day 3 down to under $80 AUD per person". On a phone, if you don't see a text box, scroll down — it sometimes hides under the keyboard. **You'll know it worked when** the new reply clearly references your previous question and feels closer to your style.

💬 Example: *"Day 2 is too packed — swap the afternoon bus tour for a slow walk through Higashiyama and a casual dinner near Gion. Keep it under ¥6,000 per person."*

## Step 4 — Ask about food, transport and neighbourhood tips

Once the day-by-day shape feels right, layer on the practical details that make a trip feel lived-in: where to eat, how to get around, and which neighbourhoods to wander in the evening. Type one focused question at a time so answers stay organised — Meta AI usually replies with short lists grouped by area, plus notes on trains, buses and walking times. One honest caveat: opening hours and prices can be a year or two out of date, especially for small local spots, so treat any specific time or dollar figure as a starting point and verify with the venue's own website before you travel. If the reply feels generic, name your hotel or district — that sharpens suggestions quickly. **You'll know it worked when** the reply includes two or three concrete recommendations you can drop straight into your notes.

💬 Example: *"We're staying near Kyoto Station. Suggest three dinner spots within a 10-minute walk — one ramen, one nicer izakaya, one vegetarian-friendly. Also: what's the easiest way to get to Arashiyama from our hotel?"*

## Step 5 — Save the plan so you don't lose it

Meta AI doesn't keep a tidy "trips" folder for you, so saving the plan is your job — and best done while the chat is still open. On a phone, scroll back through the conversation and take screenshots (Power + Volume Up on most Androids, Side Button + Volume Up on iPhones), then file them into a dedicated album called something like "Kyoto trip". On a computer, highlight the answers, copy them, and paste into a Google Doc or notes app, then tidy into one page. You can also tap the share icon inside the chat (look for an arrow pointing up, or three dots in the corner of each reply) and send the whole conversation to yourself in Messenger or email. Do this before you close the tab — clearing browser history can wipe the chat. **You'll know it worked when** you can open your phone tomorrow, swipe to the album, and read the full plan offline.

## Common mistakes

- **Giving a one-line prompt and expecting magic.** Meta AI works best when you share dates, companions and rough budget in the first message — without those, you'll get a generic answer and spend ages correcting it later. **Fix:** open with a single paragraph of context, then refine.
- **Trusting opening hours and prices as gospel.** AI suggestions can drift out of date, especially for small local spots. **Fix:** cross-check the first three places on your list with Google Maps or the venue's own site before you travel.
- **Asking five things at once.** Packing "best food, transport, day trips and hotels" into one message produces a vague, jumbled reply. **Fix:** ask one focused question per message — the conversation stays organised and each answer is more useful.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** a saved Meta AI itinerary becomes a ready-made packing and booking checklist — you can scan it the night before each day of the trip instead of fumbling with guidebooks or twelve open browser tabs.
- **For your business or work:** the same prompt-and-refine pattern works for client visits, conference trips or team off-sites — describe the goal, the people and the constraints, and let Meta AI draft an agenda you can then tweak.
- **If you're just getting started:** don't worry about getting the perfect prompt on the first try. Send a rough message, read the reply, and ask one follow-up. The plan improves with every round, and that's the whole point.

## Try it now

Open Meta AI on your phone right now and send this: *"Plan a 2-day weekend trip in my own city for one adult. I like coffee, long walks and live music. Budget under $80 AUD a day."* See what comes back — that's a 2-minute taste of how the tool thinks, and you can build on it from there.
